title: An array-or-object union cannot always be unpacked into arguments

ground_truth.statement: Argument unpacking accepts arrays and Traversable objects, not arbitrary objects. The two-int array control succeeds while stdClass, a valid object union member, raises an Error at the unpack.

allowed.reason: The object alternative includes an empty Traversable, which unpacks successfully but supplies no arguments. The runtime ArrayIterator control proves this independent arity hazard.

provenance.derivation: Upstream SKIPPED means a known bug, per InvalidCodeAnalysisTestTrait. A real union parameter replaces an asserted array local; exact tuple avoids unrelated arity issues.

notes: Upstream skips this dataset, but a deterministic runtime hazard is measurable, so it is not deferred or disabled here. PHPStan reports the noniterable unpack. Psalm is silent. Mago reports only too-few-arguments, which is correct for the empty Traversable alternative and specifically acknowledged; it still misses the distinct nontraversable hazard.
